subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a persistent `tui` plain-text accessibility profile and sponsor the narrow pi-tui selection-prefix seam required for complete coverage?
rationale: Current and shipped source prove the accessibility gap, but the public activation contract, replacement vocabulary, and dependency API direction cannot be selected safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add profile and seam
options.body: Add one documented `tui` setting with a stable ASCII symbol profile and a narrow configurable selection-prefix API in pi-tui or the OpenClaw wrapper.

options.title: Use a launch profile
options.body: Expose the same complete presentation profile through an explicit TUI launch flag if maintainers want to avoid another persisted config key.

options.title: Decline the mode
options.body: Keep the current Unicode presentation and document the terminal screen-reader limitation.

recommendation.title: Add profile and seam
recommendation.body: Add one documented `tui` setting with a stable ASCII symbol profile and a narrow configurable selection-prefix API in pi-tui or the OpenClaw wrapper.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the central tool-display behavior and has the strongest sampled history across the affected TUI and configuration surface.
